Good debate, but my take: 1) I don't think those are apt comparisons... electricity and oil are commodities at the very bottom of the stack... even AWS/cloud is a layer at the bottom, critical though it might be... intelligence is the heart of everything, at least for white collar kind of enterprises 2) not sure what the basis for saying "most businesses tend towards 10% gm"... Pfizer (pharma) is at 70%... Goldman Sachs is in the 80%... Visa at 90%+... Bloomberg, since you mentioned them is at like 40% *EBITDA* 3) for me the discussion not "RL vs not RL", more about owning your intelligence vs renting it... I do believe many (most?) enterprises will want to own at least a chunk of their intelligence... which means using open source models and customizing them in one way or another, be it through a harness, fine tuning or RL'ing... RL itself will be automated (bunch of startups working on this, Trajectory, Applied Compute, Remanence, others), with an automated feedback loop requiring no human input, so it's not going to require much expertise or effort, basically will be a solved problem... nobody is saying Global 2000 should go and hire top AI researchers

Suggérer que "le robot domestique est ici" sur la base de démos de ce type est comme dire en 2016 "la voiture autonome est ici" sur la base de démos de voiture se conduisant toute seules pendant quelques minutes. Nous sommes 10 ans plus tard, et nous n'avons toujours pas de vraies voitures autonomes (de niveau 5).

I'm definitely not "fighting the Church thesis." But, as @wtgowers pointed out, there is a question of practicality and efficiency. The real world is highly complex, messy, and not entirely predictable. It is *somewhat* predictable *IF* you accept the fact that you need to find an appropriate representation of the state of the world that allows you to make predictions by ignore much of the information about the state of the system that is simply not predictable in practice (what physicists have called entropy). For example, I can predict that the pressure in a box full of air will increase if I heat it up. This is because of the law of ideal gas pV=nRT. But there is absolutely no way in hell I can simulate the individual positions and velocities of every molecule of air in the box. Even though this is the underlying physical phenomenon with known laws, it's totally useless at a macroscopic scale, particularly for a system in interaction with the rest of the universe. So, the Church thesis, while true, is irrelevant to this discussion.

posts.title: 長興 ETERNAL（1717） 一、2Q26／1H26 財報亮點 - 毛利率創高：2Q26 毛利率 24.8%（季增 2.6ppt、年增約 4ppt），為近年新高；營業利益率亦同步走升。主因產品組合改善、油價上漲可反映至售價，加上部分低價庫存。 - 獲利大增：2Q26 稅後純益約 8.5 億元、年增約 140%，EPS 0.72 元（2022 年以來單季新高）。1H26 稅後約 12.75 億元、年增約 82%，累計 EPS 約 1.09 元。 - 營收：2Q26 合併營收約 119 億元、年增約 15%；三大事業單位（合成樹脂、電子材料、特用材料）皆成長。7–8 月營收合計約 81.6 億元，符合法人對 3Q 節奏的預期。 - 現金流／資產負債：EBITDA 約 11.7 億元，現金流維持正向。資產總額由 2025 年底約 601 億增至約 670 億（募資＋人民幣升值等）。存貨因營運量增與油價上漲而上升。借款剩餘約 18 億元；現金增資與 CB 相關作業已陸續完成。 事業別營收比重（2Q26）：合成樹脂約 51%、特用材料約 27%、電子材料約 22%。終端應用約為塗料 50%、油墨 30%、電子 20%。 二、各事業與產品組合 - 合成樹脂／特用材料是本季成長主力（特用材料年增約 24%）。產品組合優化是毛利率走升的核心原因。 - 光固化材料（UV）：全球三大原材料供應商之一。現有產能約 11 萬噸，規劃提升至 13.5–15 萬噸。年銷量約 7 萬噸，短期仍以塗料、油墨為基本盤，並拓展噴墨、交聯劑、準分子、UV 離型膜、新能源／電動車、高階 CCL、3D 列印、AI 等應用。公司估計全球光固化市場年增約 5.9%，持續取代部分熱固型材料。 - 中國與海外策略：中國仍是全球光固化原料生產重心（原料、人力、配套優勢），但產能增加、競爭升溫。公司策略為防禦中國與東南亞、聚焦高端與創新產品；歐美需求相對穩定，並布局東協、印度、拉美等高階油墨市場。 - 子公司長廣（7795）：2H26 營收預期顯著增長（ABF 設備／真空壓模機等認列高峰，上下半年認列節奏約偏後），帶動集團產品組合再改善。法人預期 3Q–4Q26 毛利率可持平或再升。 三、資本支出與擴產 董事會通過三項投資（延續 2023 年起布局）： 1. 電子材料 泰國分廠新團隊／新廠 2. 特用材料 路竹特殊製程投資（約 4.4 億元，高純度、減壓製程等，先進技術留台） 3. 與 湖北宜化成立合資（大宗如 TMP、季戊四醇），釋放蘇州／珠海產線轉向電子材料 另規劃約 20 億元台幣資本支出（智能／產能相關），自 2027 年起陸續發生。1H26 已投入約 11.7 億元，前一階段擴產大致告一段落。光固化基地現有台灣路竹、江蘇常熟、珠海等，未來亦規劃新山。 四、半導體先進材料（獨立「先進材料事業部」）
